India has made its new resident diplomatic mission in San José, Costa Rica, operational to broaden its diplomatic presence in central america and deepen bilateral engagement.Relations between India and Costa Rica have been gaining momentum, with both countries seeking to expand cooperation in trade, investment, pharmaceuticals and information technology.According to the ministry of external affairs (MEA), the Indian mission became operational on October 10.The ministry said the move would strengthen India's diplomatic outreach in central america and further consolidate ties with Costa Rica.The establishment of the resident mission is expected to facilitate closer political engagement between the two countries while promoting bilateral trade, investment and economic cooperation. Article Title: Amit Shah reaffirms India's 'zero tolerance' policy against terror
Article Text:

What is BIMSTEC?

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday called for stronger regional cooperation among BIMSTEC countries to combat terrorism , disrupt terrorist financing and organised crime, and prevent terrorist networks from finding safe havens in the region.Addressing the first Home Ministers’ Meeting of BIMSTEC countries in Delhi, Shah said India follows a policy of “zero tolerance” towards terrorism and stressed the need for collective action to strengthen regional security.“Hosting the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting is a matter of great pride and fortune for India. BIMSTEC, in a way, has become an essential platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security. With the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India is going ahead today," Shah said.We have always been committed to peace, coexistence and human welfare. We continue to be committed to these even today. India has never believed in attacking any country or establishing dominance over them. India has always believed in upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of every country and peaceful resolution of differences,” he added.Shah said the trust among BIMSTEC members was strengthened by the belief that the security arrangements of each country should contribute to the security of the others.He called for a collective resolve to ensure that terrorist networks could not find shelter, establish bases or training facilities, mobilise resources or carry out activities against other member countries.“India has always adopted a 'zero tolerance' policy against terrorism. The trust in our cooperation is strengthened by the sense that the security mechanism of every member country becomes helpful in the security of other member countries. Our mutual resolution should be to ensure that there is no scope or space for harbouring, recruiting, training, procuring resources, or carrying out activities against neighbouring nations in any part of the region,” he said.The home minister also urged member countries to cooperate on mutual legal assistance and extradition in accordance with their national laws and applicable agreements. He said such cooperation would strengthen efforts to bring criminals to justice.Highlighting counterterrorism and law enforcement as key areas of regional cooperation, Shah called for the exchange of actionable intelligence through existing nodal agencies and closer coordination to tackle terrorist financing and organised crime.He said the timely exchange of verified and actionable information on terrorists, their associates, criminal networks, financial channels and cross-border activities could strengthen collective security.Shah said efforts to curb narcotics smuggling would not succeed through the actions of individual countries alone, calling for a coordinated regional approach.“We must adopt a whole-of-region approach. The illegal proceeds from drugs provide financial strength to organised crime and are also used for terrorist financing. The diversion of precursor chemicals and transactions through the dark web make this challenge even more complex,” he said.The minister stressed that cooperation was necessary to tackle the links between drug trafficking, organised crime and terrorist financing.The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) is a regional grouping comprising seven countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.The grouping aims to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries bordering the Bay of Bengal and in its neighbourhood.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah called for stronger regional cooperation among BIMSTEC countries to combat terrorism. Shah said India follows a policy of “zero tolerance” towards terrorism and stressed the need for collective action to strengthen regional security. The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation is a regional grouping comprising seven countries.

Article Title: Last-minute question papers, more exam centres: Nandan Nilekani's plan to prevent NEET paper leaks
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Exam reforms task force head Nandan Nilekani on Tuesday suggested generating question papers at the last minute from a large question bank to reduce the risk of exam paper leaks. He also called for expanding computer-based testing across the country."Question papers create an economic incentive for them to be sold. So, the way to solve this is to really have a massive bank of questions, and only at the last minute generate the question paper for that day, and therefore the question of 'a' question paper goes away, and there's no economic incentive for that. That's one way to think about how to solve this," he said speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum.Asked whether artificial intelligence (AI) could generate exam papers on the day of a test, Nilekani replied, "Yeah. Sure. Yeah," as quoted by news agency ANI.Nilekani also stressed the need to move towards computer-based testing (CBT) for all examinations. He said India already had 150,000 locations where students could take tests, but the network needed to be expanded."The other thing is, of course, how to make sure all exams are done on a computer-based testing, and that requires a network of locations. We have 150,000 locations where a young boy or girl can take a test.That needs to be expanded," he said.Nilekani, who is heading a committee examining systemic reforms in examinations, said the panel would address these issues and indicated that the government was keen to implement its recommendations."I think these are all systemic issues which we will address in our committee. And the prime minister is very keen to implement our decisions," he said.The proposals come amid concerns over examination integrity following paper leak allegations, including those surrounding the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test ( NEET ).

CHENNAI: PM Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation for infrastructure projects worth Rs 13,000 crore in Chennai Sunday, promising Centre's support for Tamil Nadu's growth, as CM C Joseph Vijay sought funds while navigating ties with BJP-led Union govt and ally Congress."We are taking Tamil Nadu's development journey forward with CM Vijay," Modi said at IIT Madras, adding that the projects spanning Chennai Metro , roads, railways & ports would generate direct and indirect jobs. "Let us create a developed India through a developed Tamil Nadu," he said.Modi recalled his association with former Tamil Nadu CMs M Karunanidhi, J Jayalalithaa, O Panneerselvam, Edappadi K Palaniswami and MK Stalin, saying his commitment to the state remained steadfast despite changes in govt.Vijay, who hosted MP Rahul Gandhi at his home less than 24 hours earlier, shared a Metro ride and stage with Modi, signalling his intent to maintain working ties with Centre while preserving TVK's partnership with Congress. Article Title: India calls for terror acts meeting threshold to be recognised as crimes against humanity at UN
Article Text:
India's statement at the UN on terrorism and crimes against humanity

NEW DELHI: India has called for terrorist acts that meet the requisite threshold to be recognised within the framework of crimes against humanity at the United Nations.It also stressed that states must take the lead in preventing, investigating and prosecuting such crimes through their national legal and judicial systems.R Mythili, counsellor (legal adviser) at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, made the statement at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly's sixth committee during discussions on a proposed convention on the prevention and punishment of crimes against humanity.India called for the primacy of national and territorial jurisdictions, with due respect for “State sovereignty and the principle of non-interference in internal affairs”.It also said a new convention must “complement, not duplicate, existing international legal mechanisms”, cautioning against simply transferring existing international legal regimes into the proposed framework.India further called for “broadly accepted principles of international law, stronger national capacities, and transparent and inclusive negotiations” to strengthen the international framework for preventing and punishing crimes against humanity.
Article Summary: India has called for terrorist acts that meet the requisite threshold to be recognised within the framework of crimes against humanity at the United Nations. It stressed that states must take the lead in preventing, investigating and prosecuting such crimes through their national legal and judicial systems. India called for the primacy of national and territorial jurisdictions.

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday launched an attack on the Narendra Modi-led government over rising prices, alleging that people are struggling to cope with the increasing cost of food and other household essentials.Ramesh pointed to the September inflation figures, arguing that the rise in food prices deserved greater attention than the headline retail inflation rate of 5.54 per cent. Food inflation stood at 7.74 per cent during the month, while retail inflation rose from 3.40 per cent in March to 5.54 per cent in September, reaching its highest level in 23 months, according to the government data cited by him.In a post on X, Ramesh wrote, “Vote Theft is the Truth. Back-Breaking Inflation is the Reality.”The Congress leader said prices of several commonly consumed food items had surged sharply. Onions recorded a 108 per cent increase, while garlic prices rose 55 per cent, ginger became 63 per cent more expensive and lemons saw a 36 per cent rise.Describing the price increases as having “crossed all limits”, Ramesh accused the government of overlooking the difficulties faced by households.He said the pressure was not restricted to grocery bills, with transportation, education, clothing, shoes and household goods also becoming more expensive.“The impact of inflation isn’t confined to just the dinner plate. Essentials like transportation, education, clothing, shoes, and household goods are all getting more expensive,” he said.Ramesh argued that the burden of rising prices was being felt differently across income groups, with poorer households struggling to afford food and middle-class families facing pressure on their savings. He also flagged the growing burden of debt.“The poor are losing their daily bread from their plates, the middle class is seeing their savings vanish from their pockets, and the burden of debt keeps growing, but the Prime Minister is drowned in arrogance, paying no attention to the people’s troubles,” the Congress leader added.He also invoked the government's promise of “achhe din” to question its handling of the situation, alleging that the erosion of savings had accompanied the rise in prices.“The government that came to power promising ‘good days’ is not only stealing votes but also robbing savings.”Ramesh's criticism extended to the government's response to public anger over inflation and his allegations of vote theft. He claimed that the government had little incentive to address people's concerns if it did not fear losing their support.“When a vote-stealing government has no fear of the people’s anger or losing votes, why would it care about the public? That’s exactly what’s happening now. Inflation keeps rising, public outrage over vote theft keeps growing, but the Prime Minister sits there like a silent sage. Now it’s time for him to pack his bags and go,” he said.The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has projected India's economy to expand by 7 per cent in both FY26 and FY28. Its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, however, cautioned that the global economy's resilience was becoming increasingly fragile and uneven amid rising energy and food prices and geopolitical uncertainty."The global economy remains resilient, but that resilience is becoming more fragile and more uneven," the IMF said.The Fund expects the global economy to grow by 3.1 per cent in 2026 before growth improves to 3.4 per cent in 2027.Global inflation is projected to climb to 4.7 per cent in 2026, largely on account of higher energy and food prices, before easing to 4.1 per cent in 2027.
Article Summary: Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh launched an attack on the Narendra Modi-led government over rising prices. He said people are struggling to cope with the increasing cost of food and other household essentials. Food inflation stood at 7.74 per cent during the month, while retail inflation rose from 3.40 per cent in March to 5.54 per cent.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Tuesday sought an extension of the deployment of 273 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) in the national capital till October 20, citing the possibility of protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other organisations, news agency PTI reported citing sources.The deployment was scheduled to end on Monday. Article Title: Steelmaker to steer 440 crore revamp of 9 ITIs
Article Text: NEW DELHI : A Rs 440-crore overhaul will put ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India) in charge of nine govt Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in Gujarat and Andhra. The company will hold a 51% stake in entities managing the institutes under PM-SETU.Skill development ministry Monday signed shareholders' agreements covering five ITIs in Surat and four in Visakhapatnam. Rs 240 crore is earmarked for Surat and Rs 200 crore for Visakhapatnam. Centre and state govts will each hold 24.5% equity. SPVs will manage modernisation and operations. AM/NS India will implement the projects with New Age Makers' Institute of Technology as partner. Plans include modern workshops and laboratories, new trades, revised courses and more practical training.PM-SETU has Rs 60,000-crore outlay and aims to upgrade 1,000 govt ITIs and strengthen five National Skill Training Institutes. Funding includes Rs 30,000 crore from Centre, Rs 20,000 crore from states and Rs 10,000 crore from industry.
Article Summary: A Rs 440-crore overhaul will put ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India in charge of nine govt Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in Gujarat and Andhra. The company will hold a 51% stake in entities managing the institutes under PM-SETU.

Article Title: SC to government: Cap prices of non-patented medicines
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said there was no rationale for controlling the price of a few scheduled medicines and allowing the rest to be sold at inflated prices as all medicines are essential. It suggested a uniform rule limiting the MRP to not more than 16% above the price to the retailer (PTR).

SC to government: There is a great divide... why can’t you control the entire range of drugs

NEW DELHI: With the Centre failing to give even "one justification" to the satisfaction of the court in favour of patients for keeping the maximum retail price of medicines at exorbitant levels but also accepting that profit margins for drugs and medical consumables reach up to 1,000%, Supreme Court on Monday said that the price of all non-patented drugs and consumables should also be controlled and it should not be confined only to anti-cancer medicines as done by govt recently.As solicitor general Tushar Mehta and ASG Aishwarya Bhati informed SC about the decision to cap the trade margins on anti-cancer drugs at 30% of the maximum retail price, the court appreciated govt's decision but raised questions on why pricing of other medicines should not be capped. The bench pointed out various examples to drive home the point that patients are fleeced because of sky-high pricing.This relates to only cancer drugs. What about the overall? For an ordinary cardiac stent, Indian made stent, price to retailer (PTR) is Rs 5,000 but MRP is Rs 25,000... This is not even a tip of the iceberg. It (decision) has come only because of harsh observation from the court,” the bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta asked SG Tushar Mehta and also applauded his intervention resulting in a quick decision.It said the price of a drip line for saline for the retailer is Rs 11 but the MRP is around Rs 270. It said MRP for Azithromycin is Rs 78.29 but the PTS (price to stockist) is Rs 28.5.“There is a great divide... There are thousands of examples,” court said, asking govt to explain why all non-patented medicines shouldn’t be brought under price control.“Give me just one justification in favour of patients (for not controlling the prices). Why can’t you control the entire range of drugs?” the bench asked the ASG.Bhati submitted that areas with lower sales, such as rural areas, may require higher margins for the retailer so as to provide sufficient income and livelihood to the retailer, failing which the access to and availability of drugs in such areas may be adversely affected. She told the bench the Indian drug market is fairly competitive, with a large number of pharmaceutical companies in every drug segment, resulting in one of the lowest prices in the world. “If there is too much intervention by govt, it will lead to the market suffering. It will affect availability.”But court said all the justifications given by govt were not in favour of patients who had to pay the higher price. Intervening in the proceedings, the SG submitted govt was not averse to the plea and the bench also made it clear that its proceeding was only intended to “strengthen the hands of the govt and nothing else”.Govt, in its affidavit, said, “Another area of concern in the sector is supply of consumables in hospitals, where margins of 100-1000% or more are prevalent, along with a tendency of hospitals to purchase consumables that have a high MRP, with a low price to the distributor/hospital.”It admitted that patients have a very low bargaining position vis-a-vis the hospital, and a patient’s knowledge of drugs, their substitutes and their prices is also limited.“These bargaining and information asymmetries result in malpractices despite strong competition among manufacturers, leading to the need for regulation. That hospitals purchase medicines from manufacturers who provide the highest trade margin and then sell those to patients at the MRP, with margins ranging from 170% to 700% or more in the case of anti-cancer (oncology) drugs,” the affidavit said.The apex court thereafter adjourned the case for Oct 27.
Article Summary: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said there was no rationale for controlling the price of a few scheduled medicines. It suggested a uniform rule limiting the MRP to not more than 16% above the price to the retailer (PTR)SC to government: There is a great divide... why can’t you control the entire range of drugs?

Article Title: Court takes cognisance in coal block case
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A special court in Delhi took cognisance of CBI charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating and corruption against Green Infrastructure, now Athena Infraprojects, its two directors and two ex-coal ministry officials over alleged illegal 2008 allocation of Fatehpur East coal block in Chhattisgarh.It is the first cognisance of the charges in the matter since two previous judges were transferred in Aug. CBI alleged that Green Infrastructure secured the allocation by inflating its net worth from Rs 2 lakh to Rs 4,758 crore in 2006 by manipulating a loose "expression of interest" from a Malaysian firm as a formal joint venture.Spl Judge Virender Kumar Kharta found the allocation 'arbitrary and non-transparent' and flagged undue favour by then coal secretary HC Gupta and joint secretary KS Kropha.
Article Summary: CBI charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating and corruption against Green Infrastructure. Alleged illegal 2008 allocation of Fatehpur East coal block in Chhattisgarh. First cognisance of the charges in the matter since two previous judges were transferred in Aug.

Article Title: 3.85L complaints, appeals pending with 28 information commissions
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Over 3.85 lakh appeals and complaints were pending across 28 information commissions as of June 30 this year. Moreover, 14 commissions have an estimated waiting time of 1 year or more to dispose of a matter. These findings are part of the ‘Report Card on the Performance of Information Commissions in India 2025-26’ released by voluntary organisation Satark Nagrik Sangathan that brings out the report every year.The report is primarily based on an analysis of information accessed under the RTI Act from 29 information commissions across India.Data shows that 2,61,669 appeals and complaints were registered between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026, by 27 information commissions for which relevant information was available. During the same period, 2,41,627 cases were disposed of by 28 commissions.The Maharashtra State Information Commission (SIC) disposed of the highest number of cases (54,985), followed by the SICs of Karnataka (38,656), Tamil Nadu (23,808), Uttar Pradesh (21,528) and CIC (17,319).The backlog of appeals/complaints is significantly large even as it has decreased slightly in comparison to last year. The number of appeals and complaints pending on June 30, 2025, in 29 information commissions stood at over 4.13 lakh compared to this year’s figure of over 3.85 lakh for 28 commissions.At 77,000, Maharashtra SIC had the highest number of appeals and complaints pending in the country. It was followed by the Chhattisgarh SIC at over 52,000 and Bihar at over 42,000. The reporthighlights that the number of appeals and complaints pending with Central Information Commission (CIC) stood at 39,121, reflecting a significant increase from June 30, 2025 (24,102).The assessment shows that 14 commissions would take 1 year or more to dispose of an appeal/complaint filed on July 1, 2026. The estimated time required for disposal of an appeal/complaint by CIC was found to be 2 years and 3 months.Tripura SIC would take an estimated 19 years and 8 months -- a matter filed on July 1, 2026, would be disposed of in the year 2046, at the monthly rate of disposal between July 2025 and June 2026.“The long delays in disposal of cases can be attributed largely to two factors: vacancies in commissions and tardy rate of disposal by commissioners. Inordinate delays by ICs in disposing of appeals/complaints violate the basic objective of the RTI Act,” the report states.“Long delays in the commissions render the law ineffective for people, especially for those living at the margins, who are most dependent on govt services,” the report says.
Article Summary: Over 3.85 lakh appeals and complaints were pending across 28 information commissions as of June 30 this year. 14 commissions have an estimated waiting time of 1 year or more to dispose of a matter. Maharashtra State Information Commission (SIC) disposed of the highest number of cases.

Article Title: Medical errors cause 52 lakh injuries every year: Government
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An estimated 52 lakh injuries occur annually due to medical errors, including medication errors and hospital-acquired infections, according to a health ministry communication that has prompted the National Medical Commission (NMC) to push for stronger patient safety mechanisms in medical colleges and hospitals.In a notice issued last week, NMC advised all medical colleges and med institutions to appoint a patient safety nodal officer and set up a dedicated patient safety committee or cell to monitor safety practices, review incidents and recommend corrective action.Experts said medical errors are preventable lapses causing harm, ranging from wrong drugs or dosages and infections due to unsterile equipment to bedsores.The estimate was cited in a May 8 communication from additional director general of health services, which flagged the need to strengthen patient safety practices across medical colleges & hospitals.The proposed cells will cover 11 domains, including medication and surgical safety, blood transfusions, medical devices, lab and diagnostic procedures, hospital-acquired infections, antimicrobial resistance, vaccine and injection safety, and facility safety.The committees will be responsible for facilitating the reporting and analysis of patient safety incidents, near misses and high-risk events. They will identify gaps in systems, recommend corrective and preventive measures.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) is pushing for stronger patient safety mechanisms in medical colleges and hospitals. NEW DELHI: Centre has asked states and UTs to ensure hospitals prominently display rates for their services and facilities to improve transparency in treatment costs and reduce billing disputes. The directive comes even as hospital representatives question gaps in implementation.In a letter to chief secretaries of all states and UTs, health secretary Punya Salila Srivastava called for a review of compliance with applicable regulations and urged authorities to ensure rates are clearly visible and accessible to patients and attendants.Rule 9 of the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, requires hospitals covered by the law to display service rates at a conspicuous place, in the local language and English. Article Title: On cracker ban, SC says mustn't pass orders difficult to enforce
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Aware of the flagrant violation of its past Diwali cracker ban order which had specified time windows for bursting green crackers, Supreme Court on Monday refused to consider strict control over bursting of crackers and said the court must not pass orders which are difficult to implement on the ground."We have to be extremely careful in passing an order, which must be manageable and enforceable," a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said. This came in response to amicus curiae and senior advocate Aparajita Singh's plea that there could not be carte blanche for cracker bursting which, apart from causing serious pollution, adversely impacted the health of children, senior citizens and patients.The bench said, "The best way is to make people wiser, awaken them about harmful crackers and motivate them to exercise self-restraint while persuading them to return to the original tradition of lighting lamps. But sale of harmful crackers must be stopped."When the amicus said worship was part of religion and not firecrackers, and that gods would be aghast if they found that children were being harmed because of cracker bursting in their name, the bench responded, "We will not hurt religious sentiments.But at the same time, we are for the creation of an appropriate atmosphere through education and persuasion to enable people to exercise self-restraint."Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati said the regime of green crackers was already the SC's mandate. The blanket ban on cracker bursting was modified last year allowing sale of green crackers for two days and bursting for another two-day window.When the amicus focused on adverse impacts of cracker bursting, SC said, "The moment we pass a restricting order, people will take it as coercive action and react differently. We must be very practical and pragmatic in such issues. There is sufficient time for the govt to disseminate information about harmful effects of crackers and persuade them to limit it to bare minimum."Justice Bagchi said the primary concerns were health and pollution. "What will be the pollution load if people burst crackers in a short period of time?" he asked. The amicus suggested that the issue should be referred to the Commission on Air Quality Management (CAQM), which could examine the issue with the help of experts and give its suggestions to the court for passing appropriate orders.Cracker manufacturers represented by senior advocate K Parameshwar and Sai Deepak said CAQM's report could be sought on the issue. Amicus said the right to religion and right to health needed balancing as petitioners argued the right to religion every time.The court also touched upon issue of stubble burning, which has engaged the SC's attention for the last few years, and said stubble converted into bales had become commercially viable and required state support to enable farmers to shift from stubble burning.
Article Summary: Supreme Court refuses to consider strict control over bursting of crackers. Justices say the court must not pass orders which are difficult to implement on the ground. The blanket ban on cracker bursting was modified last year allowing sale of green crackers for two days.

Article Title: Delhi's new protest venue Ramlila Maidan has just 3 dates available this year - check details
Article Text:
A view of Ramlila Maidan, designated as a protest site along with two new venues,. (PTI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ramlila Maidan, newly designated as one of the capital's three protest sites, is already booked for most of the next two-and-a-half months, leaving just three days available for reservations this year.Additionally, while a small section of the ground can be used for protests free of charge, booking the larger venue, which spans 12 acres and can accommodate up to 50,000 people, involves a daily fee and a refundable security deposit.Revealing that only December 29, 30 and 31 as the availiable dates, an official quoted by PTI said, "The booking rate for the ground is Rs 50,000 per day, plus a Rs 55,000 security deposit that is refundable. The initial outlay including taxes comes to Rs 1.21 lakh for a day's booking."However, officials clarified that a small portion of the ground, with space for around 150 people, remains available for protests and gatherings free of charge.Permission to use the larger ground must be obtained from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi's horticulture department, which processes bookings after applicants secure a no-objection certificate from Delhi Police.The arrangement has drawn criticism from opposition leaders and protesters, who argue that the limited availability and high booking costs could make demonstrations difficult to organise.AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj questioned the decision, pointing to events already scheduled at the venue. Govt. played another fraud with its citizens. The Ramleela Maidan is occupied with two Ramleelas," Bharadwaj wrote on X."How can one hold a protest here? Do they want to create chaos?" he asked.Protesters also highlighted the financial burden, noting that demonstrations at Jantar Mantar did not require comparable payments.Civic officials, however, pointed to the revenue implications of allowing unrestricted use of the ground. "If given up for protest without any fees, the civic body will stand to lose at least Rs 50,000 plus per day," an official said, quoted by PTI.The ground is frequently reserved for public events and religious festivities, particularly around Dussehra and Diwali, contributing to the shortage of available dates.Apart from booking constraints, the venue presents traffic-management challenges. Located in a busy commercial area near three hospitals and municipal offices, Ramlila Maidan has witnessed major congestion during political rallies and other large gatherings.Officials said police often have to introduce one-way traffic restrictions on Asaf Ali Road and divert vehicles towards Jawaharlal Nehru Marg. A BJP rally in 2014 reportedly caused traffic jams extending nearly four kilometres to ITO, despite being held on a Sunday.The venue has been central to Delhi's political history for decades. Once a pond, the site was filled and levelled around 1930 to accommodate Ramlila performances, which began there in 1932. It subsequently hosted major political gatherings addressed by leaders including Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Jayaprakash Narayan and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.On June 25, 1975, the day the Emergency was declared, Jayaprakash Narayan and Vajpayee addressed a rally at the ground. Relatively recently, Arvind Kejriwal took oath as Delhi chief minister there in 2013.The controversy follows an standing order issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, which removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues and identified Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as the three new locations for demonstrations. Police said a detailed, revised standard operating procedure for protests at these sites would be issued separately.
Article Summary: Just three days available for reservations this year at Ramlila Maidan. A small section of the ground can be used for protests free of charge. But booking the larger venue involves a daily fee and a refundable security deposit. The arrangement has drawn criticism from opposition leaders and protesters.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: In 2012, Taylor Swift pledged $4 million for a Nashville education centre; 14 years later, the space is showcasing artwork by local schoolchildren and artists with developmental disabilities
Article Text:
Taylor Swift

A major gift for education

Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ mansion: Inside the $47 million Beverly Hills home where her music video was filmed(Image Credit: Instagram)

Learning by making

Two groups, one exhibition

A centre still doing its job

From a pledge to a public platform

Taylor Swift’s $4 million gift to the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum in 2012 helped create a dedicated education centre in Nashville. The space was designed for more than music lessons: it would give children and families room to learn, experiment and engage with country music’s history. Fourteen years later, the centre is hosting Connection, an exhibition of posters created by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists from Friends Life Community, a nonprofit serving adults with developmental disabilities. The museum says the participants explored the history and techniques of Hatch Show Print, its historic letterpress shop, before making their own work. The exhibition brings the centre’s original educational promise to life, showing how a space built for learning can keep opening doors to creativity and community.In May 2012, Swift pledged $4 million towards a new education centre at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. According to MusicRow, it was the largest capital contribution by an individual artist in the museum’s 45-year history at the time. The museum named the centre in her honour.The gift formed part of a wider expansion campaign called 'Working on a Building: Country Music Lives Here'. The museum planned to grow from 140,000 square feet to more than 350,000 square feet, creating additional exhibition and learning spaces as well as new visitor facilities.The Taylor Swift Education Center was planned as a space of more than 7,500 square feet, spread across parts of two floors. Its design included three classrooms and a children’s exhibition gallery. The museum expected its new facilities to increase its educational capacity by as much as sevenfold.The planned classrooms were intended for a range of activities, from the museum’s flagship Words & Music programme to family events and distance learning. One “wet classroom” was designed for hands-on projects that could get messy, including letterpress art activities connected to Hatch Show Print.The centre’s original vision was not limited to traditional classroom instruction. The museum planned spaces where students could explore objects, observe curators at work and take part in activities that made music history tangible. A visible storage area and design studio would allow visitors to see how museum professionals handle and interpret collections.That hands-on approach is reflected in the centre’s current exhibition, Connection. Opened in 2026, the show brings together posters made by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists engaged with Friends Life Community. The project began with visits to Hatch Show Print, the museum’s nearly 150-year-old letterpress shop. Students learned about the shop’s history, studied design principles and explored how letterpress printing works. They then created shapes using foam and sponges, printed those forms and used them as inspiration for their finished posters, as per reports.The process gave participants a chance to learn not only by looking at art, but by making it. They experimented with words, images, colour and composition, using the print shop’s techniques to develop their own visual ideas.The exhibition also grew from a collaboration between the museum and Friends Life Community, which serves adults with developmental disabilities. Friends Life invited Hatch Show Print Master Printer Emeritus Jim Sherraden to work as a teaching artist in residence in 2023. In late 2024, artists from Friends Life Community visited the print shop for a behind-the-presses tour. Sherraden and Jennifer Haston, the organisation’s visual arts programme coordinator, helped participants bring their words, lettering and images to life through poster-making, as per reports.The posters created by both groups form the exhibition’s central focus. The museum says the works use action words and imagery to imagine a future where people connect through creative art and social causes. The title Connection speaks to the ideas behind the exhibition, but also to the relationships built through the process: between students and artists, participants and printers, and the public and the museum.The project demonstrates how a museum education space can bring people together across ages and abilities. It also gives visitors the opportunity to encounter work made by members of their own community, rather than only by established artists or historical figures.When Swift made her pledge, the museum described the centre as a place for school groups, families, young people and adults. The new exhibition shows how that original ambition continues to shape the space more than a decade later.The education centre is not simply a room named after a famous musician. It is part of the museum’s broader effort to connect people with country music and its creative traditions through participation. In Connection, that means learning about letterpress printing, trying the process and producing posters that reflect the creators’ own ideas.The exhibition is open to museum visitors, with admission included in the price of a museum ticket. The museum also offers free admission for local youth and discounted tickets for up to two accompanying adults from Davidson County and neighbouring counties, with proof of residency.Swift’s generous contribution of $4 million played a crucial role in creating a lasting educational component within one of Nashville’s most iconic cultural institutions. The carefully designed classrooms, a dedicated children’s gallery, and interactive programming were all put in place with the intention of transforming the museum into more than just a location for viewing exhibitions. These elements were strategically crafted to provide visitors with opportunities to learn through hands-on experiences and active participation.Fast forward a remarkable fourteen years, and the vibrant and eye-catching posters showcased in the current exhibition, aptly titled Connection, stand as a compelling testament to that original vision which has been successfully brought to life. Local students, in collaboration with talented artists who have developmental disabilities, have engaged deeply in the exploration of a historic printing tradition. They have successfully harnessed this medium to express and convey their unique perspectives and personal narratives.However, it is important to note that this exhibition does not represent the conclusion of the center's evolving narrative. Instead, it serves to illustrate the extraordinary outcomes that can arise when a cultural institution commits resources and efforts toward creating a dedicated physical space, fostering educational opportunities, and promoting creative accessibility over an extended timeframe. A generous gift made in 2012 laid a solid foundation for establishing this creative setting; now, the individuals who engage with it today are actively populating that environment with their own creative works, innovative ideas, and meaningful connections.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments section below.
Article Summary: In May 2012, Swift pledged $4 million towards a new education centre at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum in Nashville. Fourteen years later, the centre is hosting Connection, an exhibition of posters created by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists from Friends Life Community.

Article Title: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman avoids commitment on LTCG, STT changes ahead of Budget
Article Text:
File photo: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

SBI Research proposes scrapping LTCG tax on equities

Sitharaman says RBI focused on curbing rupee volatility

Finance minister highlights investment opportunities

Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday declined to indicate whether the government would make changes to long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax or securities transaction tax (STT), saying it was too early to comment as preparations for the upcoming Union Budget had begun.Replying to a question at an event, Sitharaman said investors in India and abroad had been discussing the taxation of capital gains and different asset classes and the government was open to hearing their views.“We are very close to the budget and the preparation for the budget has started, and it may not be the best time for me to say what I will or what I will not consider,” she said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, as cited by news agency ANI.Her remarks come a day after a report by SBI Research proposed abolishing LTCG tax on equity investments to encourage longer-term investments and help stabilise foreign capital flows.SBI Research has called on the government to consider extending the holding period for equity investments to two or three years while abolishing LTCG tax on equities.“The government must seriously look into anchoring hot money flows into equity segment by extending the holding period to say 2-3 years and abolishing the long-term capital gains tax for equity,” the report said.The proposal comes amid sustained foreign portfolio investor (FPI) selling in Indian equities.According to figures cited in the report, foreign investors sold shares worth Rs 44,166 crore in October up to the time of publication, taking their total equity withdrawals in 2026 to Rs 3.04 lakh crore.The current LTCG tax rate for foreign investors on equity investments is 12.5 per cent. The Union Budget 2026 retained this rate for listed shares and equity mutual funds, continuing the framework introduced in 2024.SBI Research also called for simplifying the repatriation of export earnings, suggesting a reasonable timeframe of around six months, and sought greater clarity on withholding tax applicable to external commercial borrowings.At the event, Sitharaman also addressed the rupee's depreciation against the US dollar, saying the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was focused on limiting excessive volatility rather than fixing the currency at a particular level.She acknowledged that the rupee had depreciated significantly over the past 18 months, attributing much of the pressure to external challenges. She said India's economic fundamentals and foreign exchange reserves remained sound.“They are not trying to fix the rupee. They are trying to stop the volatility. And for that, there is a lot of effort from the RBI side. So, these efforts from the RBI... will continue not to...fix the rupee. We would appreciate it if the rupee finds its own (value),” she said, according to news agency PTI.Sitharaman's comments followed a series of measures announced by the RBI to curb pressure on the domestic currency. These included a special window for oil marketing companies to meet dollar demand outside the spot market and tighter rules for foreign exchange derivatives trading.The central bank also introduced a reserve requirement linked to certain dollar purchases.The measures supported the rupee, which rose around 1 per cent on Monday. The currency appreciated to Rs 94.96 against the US dollar in early trade on Tuesday.“I'm sure there are efforts which the RBI would take further to make sure that the rupee doesn't become too volatile,” Sitharaman said, adding that India's economic fundamentals remained sound.She also reiterated the government's commitment to fiscal discipline and macroeconomic stability, while maintaining spending priorities in welfare, education and healthcare.Sitharaman also outlined investment opportunities in infrastructure, semiconductors, renewable energy and emerging technologies.On semiconductor manufacturing, she defended India's approach of developing both advanced chips and those used in everyday applications, including refrigerators, automobiles, industrial machinery and Internet of Things devices.She said the expansion of artificial intelligence and data centres would require substantial electricity generation, reliable power infrastructure and sustainable sources of green energy.Investments in transmission networks and renewable energy would be important to meet these requirements.The finance minister said the National Infrastructure Pipeline had grown to more than USD 4.5 trillion, offering opportunities across sectors and regions.She also highlighted the role of the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development and the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund in mobilising long-term capital.Sitharaman further said domestic private investment was gaining momentum in areas including renewable energy, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities.She noted that India's civil aviation sector was growing at around 16 per cent, creating additional investment opportunities in aviation-related infrastructure and services.
Article Summary: SBI Research proposes abolishing LTCG tax on equity investments. Nirmala Sitharaman says it is too early to comment as preparations for the upcoming Union Budget have begun. She acknowledged that the rupee had depreciated significantly over the past 18 months, attributing much of the pressure to external challenges.

Article Title: Want a home in Delhi? DDA offers 2,516 flats at 25% off
Article Text:
Delhi Development Authority is initiating a new housing scheme for low-income group flats in Narela

Article Title: MDR on UPI transactions over Rs 2,000 deferred; to come into effect post Diwali
Article Text:
Govt defers 0.4% merchant discount rate on UPI payments

MUMBAI: Its official. There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over. The National Payment’s Corporation of India’s The UPI and Services Steering Committee has deferred the implementation of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select person-to-merchant UPI transactions until immediately after Diwali, citing the festive season. The implementation date will be notified separately.The Times of India had reported last week that finance ministry and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) have decided to defer the introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions, seeking to avoid adding to business costs and hitting consumption at a time of economic headwinds, people aware of the matter said. The revised rollout was expected to be pushed to January 2027 from October 15. However,the announcement on Tuesday states that the implementation will be immediately after Diwali.The MDR framework was approved and notified by NPCI on September 15, with a 0.4% charge for eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. The framework was to take effect from October 15, giving banks, payment aggregators and other ecosystem participants a month to make operational changes.Also read: Pakistan angle under probe? Delhi Police files 4 FIRs over fake posts since Oct 10 The decision to defer the rollout comes just days before the scheduled start and follows demands from trade bodies and merchant associations for a January implementation. They have argued that introducing the fee during the festive season, when retail activity and digital payments typically rise, could increase costs for merchants and weigh on sales.The framework was designed to create a revenue stream for the payments ecosystem after more than six years of effectively zero MDR on UPI. The government had said the levy would apply only to specified merchant transactions, with payments up to Rs 2,000 and eligible small merchants continuing to remain free. About 96% of P2M transactions were expected to remain unaffected.The deferment gives merchants and payment companies more time to prepare while allowing the government to avoid introducing a new transaction cost at a potentially sensitive point for consumption.
Article Summary: There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over. The revised rollout was expected to be pushed to January 2027 from October 15. The announcement on Tuesday states that the implementation will be immediately after Diwali. The MDR framework was approved and notified by NPCI on September 15.
