Tech Mahindra and Infosys also rose by approximately 3% each.FM Nirmala Sitharaman said on Tuesday that discussions have been underway in domestic and international forums on long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax (STT). Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, she noted that both Indian and international investors had been sharing their views on LTCG tax. She added that the debate over transaction tax and whether different asset classes should be taxed in a similar manner had been discussed extensively.Though she refrained from committing to any changes.“We are very close to the budget and the preparation for the budget has started, and it may not be the best time for me to say what I will or what I will not consider,” she said.Her remarks come as India's equity market continues to face substantial outflows amid several challenges. In its Ecowrap report on Monday, SBI Research said the government should consider scrapping LTCG tax on equities, arguing that the move could encourage investors to hold their investments for longer.Heavyweight IT stocks surged, helping lift the broader market despite the prevailing headwinds. The decline in global AI-linked stocks has also improved sentiment towards India's prominent technology companies, which have increasingly been viewed as an ‘anti-AI’ trade.South Korea's Kospi, considered a key reflection of the artificial intelligence investment boom, plunged more than 6%, while Japan's Nikkei fell over 2%. Major technology stocks, including Samsung, also suffered steep losses as concerns grew over excessive optimism surrounding the emerging technology. Analysts have warned that the AI rally could be developing into a bubble.The rupee strengthened by 82 paise to 94.96 against the US dollar in early trade on Tuesday, extending its recovery following measures announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to support the weakening currency.On Monday, the RBI tightened regulations governing rupee non-deliverable derivative contracts, restricting overseas clients to using these instruments only for hedging. It also extended a 20% cash reserve requirement to banks' own rupee currency hedges.These steps followed four measures announced by the central bank on Saturday. They included a dedicated dollar supply window for three state-run oil companies, tighter curbs on foreign exchange derivatives, a 20% cash reserve requirement for certain currency contracts and stricter daily cash reserve requirements for banks.“These steps are expected to reduce pressure on the spot market and curb speculative dollar buying, supporting the currency in the near term. However, sustained recovery will depend on FII flows, crude oil prices and broader dollar movement,” said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst of Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities.After climbing to multi-year peaks, bond yields edged lower, providing some relief to equity markets. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury slipped below 5.2%, while the 30-year Treasury yield declined to 5.56%.The yield on two-year US Treasury bonds, which tends to track expectations around Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, also eased below 4.8%.Rising bond yields have recently weighed on stock markets because higher returns from debt instruments can make them more attractive to investors, diverting funds away from equities, particularly in emerging markets. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, meaning a sharp rise in yields indicates a selloff in the bond market.ALSO READ: Will Budget bring LTCG, STT relief? Here’s what FM Nirmala Sitharaman said Crude oil prices fell on Tuesday as investors weighed the possibility of additional Russian oil supplies reaching global markets. US President Donald Trump defended his administration's decision to temporarily relax restrictions on Russian diesel supplies.Brent crude futures dropped more than 1%, trading near $105 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also declined by over 1% to below $93 per barrel.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex ended the day at 73,033.78, up 1,109 points or 1.54%. Nifty50 closed at 22,721.95, up 359 points or1.60%. The rally added more than Rs 4.12 lakh crore to the combined market capitalisation of listed companies. The rupee strengthened by 82 paise to 94.96 against the US dollar in early trade.

Article Title: As Anthropic and OpenAI are set for IPOs, Broadcom CEO has a message for AI investors: For now, it is still losing money
Article Text:
Anthropic

‘Like they are in a casino’

With frontier artificial intelligence (AI) labs Anthropic and OpenAI moving toward historic Initial Public Offerings (IPO), Broadcom CEO Hock Tan has issued a blunt warning to AI investors: despite the towering valuations, the generative AI sector remains an unprofitable endeavour. Speaking at an industry gathering in Singapore organised by DBS Bank, the leader of the $1.7 trillion semiconductor supplier framed AI as a volatile and uncertain financial bet at current times.“For now, it’s still losing money,” Tan said of the AI sector, adding, “So frankly, it doesn’t tell anything at this point except that there is a lot of potential revenue growth out of providing frontier generative AI models.”Anthropic is expected to list publicly around Thanksgiving, targeting a valuation in the $2 trillion territory, with OpenAI projected to follow closely behind. Both companies are depending on a vast international build-out of data centres, semiconductor wafers, advanced processor manufacturing and cloud computing capacity to fulfill market demand and eventually turn a profit.Tan warned that a looming shortage of investment capital will likely form the industry's next major roadblock to continued expansion.The assessment comes from an executive whose company directly finances its growth by supplying essential hardware components for the AI boom, with Broadcom's equity rising nearly 10% this year. Tan argued that many market participants are pouring money into technologies they fundamentally fail to grasp, comparing enterprise spending behavior to children wasting coins in an arcade.“A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in,” Tan remarked, according to Bloomberg. They “set very extreme expectations only to find out that it’s almost like they are in a casino.”“When you are a kid, you go to a video arcade, you play. Your parents give you $10 of tokens, you finish it in 10 minutes and you haven’t learned anything. That’s what happening in enterprises today,” he added.Sharing the stage alongside Tan, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan voiced similar caution regarding infrastructure limits. He noted that physical hardware supplies will remain constrained over the next few years, warning that memory chip shortages could become the first segment within the broader AI ecosystem to experience a slowdown.
Article Summary: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warns that the generative AI sector remains unprofitable. Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward historic Initial Public Offerings (IPO) Both companies are depending on a vast international build-out of data centres, semiconductor wafers, advanced processor manufacturing and cloud computing capacity.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu warns employees of tough times ahead says no hike this year, trying to avoid layoffs
Article Text:
ZOHO Founder Sridhar Vembu

No salary hikes at Zoho this year

We will work hard to avoid mass layoffs: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu

Read Sridhar Vembu’s complete post here

The business outlook for software is uncertain and AI has raised costs dramatically with a) massive 4-fold increase in server prices which we need for data centers b) AI usage increasing rapidly, leading to much higher expenses, which we are trying to control.

On top of that is the challenging geopolitical backdrop.

We have cut down on our marketing budget. We have also told our employees that we cannot have our usual pay increase this year. I have apolgized for not being able to avoid this.

We will work hard to avoid mass layoffs but the outlook for software jobs in general is grim. We have not been growing our employee count for 18 months now.

Most of our employees understand the situation. I am thankful to them.

We are in the middle of reinventing ourselves. The next 3-5 years will decide how our reinvention has worked. Please pray for us

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has informed the employees that they will not receive the company’s usual annual salary hikes this year, as the company grapples with the increasing costs related to artificial intelligence and the uncertain business environment and global geopolitical challenges. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Vembu said that the outlook for the software industry remains uncertain and that AI has significantly increased operating expenses for companies such as Zoho. As per Vembu, the server prices required for data centers have surged four-fold, while increasing usage of AI tools has led to much higher expenses that the company is attempting to control. He also added that these pressures have been compounded by a challenging geopolitical backdrop.As part of its efforts to manage costs, Zoho has reduced its marketing budget and paused annual salary increases for employees. Vembu said the decision was difficult and acknowledged that he had apologised to employees for not being able to avoid suspending pay hikes this year. The comments offer a rare glimpse into the financial pressures faced by software companies as they invest heavily in AI infrastructure while navigating an increasingly competitive technology landscape.While warning that the broader outlook for software jobs is "grim", Vembu stressed that Zoho is trying to avoid large-scale workforce reductions. "We will work hard to avoid mass layoffs," he said, even as he cautioned that employment prospects across the software sector are becoming more challenging.Vembu also revealed that Zoho has not increased its employee headcount for the last 18 months, signalling a prolonged hiring slowdown at the Chennai-headquartered software company. He added that most employees understand the situation and expressed gratitude for their support during a difficult period
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has informed employees that they will not receive the company’s usual annual salary hikes this year. He said that the outlook for the software industry remains uncertain and that AI has significantly increased operating expenses for companies such as Zoho. The comments offer a rare glimpse into the financial pressures faced by software companies.

Article Title: Kroger, one of America's oldest grocery chain to layoff thousands; largest in its 143-year history, here's what CEO told employees at townhall
Article Text:
What CEO Greg Foran told employees at townhall

Albertsons wants Kroger to pay $9 billion over failed Kroger deal

America's oldest retail chain Kroger Co plans to eliminate roughly 3,000 corporate positions over the next three years, marking a sweeping workforce reduction as new Chief Executive Officer Greg Foran moves to overhaul the grocer’s management structure. The cuts represent more than one-third of Kroger’s approximately 8,200 corporate staff, making the restructuring one of the largest corporate employees' reductions in the supermarket chain’s 143-year history.Foran, a former Walmart executive, who joined the retailer in February this year, detailed the turnaround strategy in a memo to employees following a companywide meeting on Monday, October 12. The restructuring comes as America's largest traditional grocer contends with slowing top-line growth, fierce retail competition, and persistent inflationary pressures impacting consumer spending. The memo outlined plans to eliminate redundant functions across departments while modernizing daily operations. Kroger is increasingly turning to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to automate workflows and drive efficiencies across its corporate network.The Cincinnati-based grocery giant announced the layoffs to its employees during an all-company call Monday, October 12. In the memo sent to Kroger employees obtained by the Business Courier, CEO Greg Foran wrote that the company’s transformation will result in the company reducing its corporate workforce across multiple functions by about 3,000 roles.The moves would take Kroger from having about 8,200 corporate workforce employees to roughly 5,200.“As a company, we have made great progress on many fronts with our customers. We started reducing prices and improving our customer experience in stores and online, and we made investments in simplifying our associates’ lives through technology,” Foran wrote. “Our business is becoming leaner, more focused and more competitive. We are working to be more agile; more precise in our execution; and deliver benefits to our customers, associates and our shareholders. ”CEO Foran reportedly said that the changes are intended to reduce duplicative work, lower prices and redirect investment toward store employees as the grocer integrates AI into workflows. Kroger expects to start sharing details about the affected roles in the coming months. The reductions will help the company put more resources toward cutting prices, improving shopping experience and investing in frontline employees, Foran wrote in the memo.Foran, who helped turn around Walmart’s US business in the mid- to late 2010s, is implementing Kroger’s biggest price cuts in years, while making service in stores friendlier and faster. The operator of Fred Meyer and Ralphs chains is also taking a more aggressive approach toward supplier negotiations. The company laid off nearly 1,000 corporate employees last year to cut costs.The three-year downsizing marks the latest decisive shift under Foran's leadership as Kroger works to defend its market share against deep-discount rivals and major big-box retailers.Incidentally, the layoffs come at the same time when rival grocery chain Albertsons Cos is demanding that Kroger Co pay more than $9 billion for the collapse of the largest US grocery chain merger in history. Albertsons claims Kroger "willfully breached" its contractual commitments and should pay more than $9.3 billion, including a premium stockholders would have gotten and a $600 million termination fee.
Article Summary: Kroger Co plans to eliminate roughly 3,000 corporate positions over the next three years. The cuts represent more than one-third of Kroger’s approximately 8,200 corporate staff, making the restructuring one of the largest corporate employees' reductions in the supermarket chain's 143-year history. Kroger expects to start sharing details about the affected roles in the coming months.

Article Title: Silicon Valley is facing a 'huge shortage' that has made Dario Amodei make telephone call to Alexandr Wang, Demis Hassabis 'upset' and Elon Musk partner with the company he openly 'trashed' days befor
Article Text:
Elon Musk publicly reverses his stand on Anthropic, days after slamming it

Anthropic's Dario Amodei knocks at rival Meta's door

A global shortage of raw computing power is upending Silicon Valley, sparking bitter corporate turf wars, sending executives on worldwide scrambles for hardware, and forging improbable alliances between fierce rivals, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal (WSJ). The fierce bottleneck has become the tech industry's central battleground, reshaping executive suites and imperiling the prospects of up-and-coming startups that cannot secure enough chips to keep pace.According to a WSJ report, the severity of the compute crunch was laid bare inside Google, which spent $2.7 billion in 2024 to rehire pioneering researcher Noam Shazeer to steer key projects like its flagship Gemini models. Despite the enormous price tag, Google failed to guarantee Shazeer the computing capacity he sought. After internal reallocations cut his team’s resources in favor of another initiative, Shazeer departed for rival OpenAI, highlighting an internal environment where researchers frequently quarrel over processing power. The Journal reported that Google co-founder Sergey Brin has at times overridden formal allocation procedures to divert compute to his preferred projects, while DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis has expressed frustration over a lack of resources dedicated to fundamental, long-term research.According to an earlier report in CNBC, "One of the biggest points of friction inside Google is compute." The report added, "Google is investing more than almost any company in the world in data centers, chips and related infrastructure. But capacity remains scarce. Every TPU assigned to training a model, serving a Google product, or fulfilling a contract with a cloud customer reflects a choice among competing priorities. " Claiming sources it further said that frustrations over access to compute can be especially acute when Google announces large infrastructure commitments to competing labs like Anthropic, whose models compete directly with Gemini.The scramble for capacity has driven competitors into surprising pacts, most notably between Anthropic and Elon Musk's xAI. Facing severe infrastructure strain and outages triggered by the runaway popularity of its Claude Code assistant, Anthropic dispatched co-founder Tom Brown to xAI’s offices in Hawthorne, California, in late March to negotiate renting compute directly from Musk’s venture. The talks paved the way for Anthropic to lease over 300 megawatts of computing power through an agreement connected to Musk’s company, a deal valued at up to $45 billion. The alliance bridged an ideological divide between Musk and Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei. Just days before the partnership, Elon Musk, in a post on X, wrote, ""Your AI hates Whites & Asians, especially Chinese, heterosexuals and men. This is misanthropic and evil," Musk wrote. "Fix it."Amodei also reportedly approached Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang in search of excess capacity. According to the report, "Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei also spoke on the phone with Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang earlier this year, attempting to source more computing capacity, according to a person familiar with the matter. Meta debated whether to give chips to Anthropic and ultimately decided not to for now, people familiar with the matter said. "Across the wider tech sector, the hunt for computational power resembles a frantic gold rush. Intermediaries like San Francisco Compute are scouring unconventional sites worldwide to locate usable clusters, finding servers running in places as unusual as a converted chicken coop in rural America or navigating monsoon floods in Manila to source hardware in Taipei. Simultaneously, the market has swung aggressively in favor of suppliers: the hourly cost to rent Nvidia H100 chips on one-year contracts jumped 60 percent over the past year, while cloud providers now routinely demand multiyear leases and massive upfront down payments.
Article Summary: Anthropic's Dario Amodei knocks at rival Meta's door in search of more computing power. Google spent $2.7 billion in 2024 to rehire pioneering researcher Noam Shazeer to steer key projects like its flagship Gemini models. The scramble for capacity has driven competitors into surprising pacts.

Article Title: AI company that Elon Musk’s xAI and Meta once 'fought' to partner with has filed for bankruptcy, says will have to shut down if ...
Article Text:
When Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI 'fought' to partner with Character.ai

Character.AI faced lawsuits over its chatbots encouraging users to do 'dangerous things'

In early 2024, two of the biggest Silicon Valley companies -- Elon Musk's xAI and Meta -- fought to partner with a Generative AI company. Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI competed for tie-up with chatbot-maker Character.ai, as deep-pocketed technology companies swarmed around the hottest artificial intelligence startups in Silicon Valley. Two years later, the same hotshot AI company, Character.ai, has filed for bankruptcy.Character.AI said on Monday it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US. In a statement, dated October 12, the company said, "Today, we’re sharing that Character.ai has initiated a voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy process to facilitate a court-supervised sale of the company." The AI company said that it has begun the formal ​process to sell assets, including a license ​of certain intellectual property, through Chapter 11 and is ⁠seeking court approval for auction rules that would designate ​Disney as the lead, or stalking horse, bidder.Under this process, Disney's bid would set a baseline offer while allowing competing bidders to submit higher bids, and the company expects the sale process to conclude by late November or early December 2026. “After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the ‌board ⁠determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders," said Colin Adams, CEO of Character.AI.Character Technologies has listed estimated assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million, according ​to a court filing. The company said that it ​intends ⁠to continue operating its business, including the Character.AI platform, with minimal service disruptions during the sale process. If the ⁠process ​fails to produce a buyer ​willing to continue operating the platform, it will be shut down.According to a report in Financial Times, in May 2024, Meta and Elon Musk’s xAI sought partnership with chatbot-maker Character.ai. Facebook owner Meta reportedly held early discussions over a tie-up with Character.ai, which uses large language models to generate conversation in the style of various figures and personas, according to four people familiar with the matter. The groups discussed their top researchers working closely together on initiatives such as pre-training and developing models, said the report quoting sources.Character.ai also held exploratory talks with xAI over a similar partnership. Report claimed that the talks were focused on advancing research rather than an acquisition.Character.AI was founded by two former Google employees. In 2024, Google licensed the company’s technology and rehired the executives to work on generative AI products. A spokesman for Alphabet said that said the ⁠company played ​no role in developing Character.AI's products.Earlier this year, a filing by Kentucky’s attorney general in a lawsuit claimed that Chatbots created by AI companion company Character.AI sometimes advised users to cut, starve or kill themselves. The lawsuit was filed in January with many specific allegations against the company blacked out. It alleged that the company’s products “were designed to entice children in ​a manner that prioritizes engagement over child wellbeing” and “encourages suicide, self-injury, isolation, and psychological manipulation. ”The lawsuit calls Character.AI’s products defective. “Defendants have subjected Kentucky's children and residents to ​an ill-planned, uncontrolled ⁠experiment without any—let alone adequate or effective—safety measures,” it alleges.
Article Summary: Character.ai faced lawsuits over its chatbots encouraging users to do 'dangerous things' In early 2024, two of the biggest Silicon Valley companies -- Elon Musk's xAI and Meta -- fought to partner with a Generative AI company. Facebook owner Meta reportedly held early discussions over a tie-up with Character.ai.
